item.title: Stateless AI Agents Are the Real Problem
item.content:encoded: AI agents don’t actually learn from experience, they reset after every run. Chat history is not real memory and doesn’t scale well. Without memory, agents keep repeating the same mistakes and rediscovering solutions. A simple memory layer can store facts, past events, and learned steps. Even basic memory makes agents more consistent and efficient over time. You don’t need complex systems, just enough memory to retain what worked and what didn’t.

item.title: Where Is Africa in Jensen Huang’s Five-Layer AI Cake?
item.content:encoded:
Africa isn’t one country, but it shares the same structural gaps: energy, water, education. Ethiopia shows what’s possible with sovereign energy investment.
Jensen Huang’s five-layer AI model highlights a hard truth: Africa mostly consumes, it doesn’t build. China proves energy is the real competitive edge. No energy, no development. No development, no tech. No tech, no AI.
The path forward is simple: build power, cut bureaucracy, get pragmatic or stay behind.

His consciousness drifts into space, observing Earth and the cosmos with cold clarity. As time and perception distort, he confronts existence itself—only to awaken and realize he survived, forever changed by the experience.

item.title: AI’s Critical Role in Healthcare and Online Safety

While AI introduces new risks, it also provides the strongest defense—making “safety by design” and large-scale deployment essential for protecting vulnerable populations.

item.title: A New York Times Investigation Named Its Satoshi

item.title: How Zodia Custody's BitMEX Integration Quietly Rewires Institutional Crypto Market Structure
item.content:encoded: BitMEX, the exchange that invented the perpetual swap, is now live on Zodia Custody's Interchange off-venue settlement network.
